---
applyTo: "app/actions/**/*.rb"
---

# Actions

- Write an action for one task that could be run from more than one place, e.g. a form, a job, the console or a rake task, and put it in `app/actions/`, e.g. `Posts::ArchivePost` in `app/actions/posts/archive_post.rb`.
- Keep actions separate from command forms. A command form handles what the user submits and returns the resource or `false`, e.g. `PublishPostForm`. An action is its own object that does a task, e.g. `Posts::ArchivePost`.
- Keep calls from one action to another rare. Call another action only when it is part of the same task, and no caller would want one without the other.
- When the work needs more than one step, run the steps from a job, not from an action. Enqueue a job for a later step that can wait, e.g. `Posts::PublishPost.call(post, publisher: post.scheduled_by)` then `NotifySubscribersJob.perform_later(post)` in `PublishScheduledPostJob`. Keep `Posts::PublishPost` to publishing the post.
- An action MAY enqueue a job, e.g. `NotifySubscribersJob.perform_later(post)`. When it enqueues inside a transaction, make sure the job waits for the commit, e.g. with `self.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = true` in the job class.
- When enqueuing takes more than calling the job with what the caller has, put it in an action whose name starts with `Enqueue`, e.g. when it enqueues one job for each post in a collection, as `Posts::EnqueuePublishes` does with `posts.find_each { |post| PublishScheduledPostJob.perform_later_for(post) }`, or works out the job's arguments from the records it's given, as `Posts::EnqueueStatsRefresh` does with `RefreshNewsletterStatsJob.perform_later(post.newsletter_id)`. When the caller already has the job's arguments, call the job in the caller, e.g. `PublishScheduledPostJob.perform_later_for(post)`.
- You SHOULD NOT pick a job's queue in the caller with `set(queue:)`, e.g. `NotifySubscribersJob.set(queue: :high).perform_later(post)`. When the queue depends on the job's arguments, use a `queue_as` block in the job.
- When an action calls another action, rescue the other action's error and raise your own, e.g. `rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, Posts::UnpublishPost::Error => e` then `raise Error, e.message` in `Posts::ArchivePost`. You MUST NOT let another action's error escape your action.
- Raise the error for the same cause, e.g. `rescue Posts::SendNewsletter::ServiceError => e` then `raise ServiceError, e.message`, not `raise Error`. Put that `rescue` before the one for the other action's `Error`.
- If an action needs to carry on when another action it calls fails, you MUST NOT call that action from it. Run it as a separate step from a job.
- Put each action in a module named after the resource it works on, in the plural, e.g. `Posts`. Name the action after the task, starting with a verb. The name can include the resource, e.g. `Posts::ArchivePost`, not `ArchivePost` or `Posts::ArchivePostAction`.
- Inherit every action from `ApplicationAction` in `app/actions/application_action.rb`. Give each action an `initialize` that keeps its arguments in private `attr_reader`s, and an instance method `call` that does the task.
- Write the parts of an action in this order, without comment headings: error classes, `include` lines, validations, `initialize`, `call`, then `private` with the `attr_reader`s followed by any private methods, e.g. `class Error < StandardError; end`, `include ValidatedCallable`, `validates :post, :publisher, ...`, `def initialize(post, publisher:)`, `def call` and `attr_reader :post, :publisher` in `Posts::PublishPost`.
- Call an action with the class method, e.g. `Posts::ArchivePost.call(post)`, not `Posts::ArchivePost.new(post).call`.
- Pass an action the records it works on, not their IDs, e.g. `Posts::ArchivePost.call(post)`, not `Posts::ArchivePost.call(post.id)`. Find the records in the caller, e.g. a controller loads the post. You MUST NOT look a record up by ID inside an action.
- Make the resource an action works on its first positional argument, and pass every other argument as a keyword, e.g. `Posts::PublishPost.call(post, publisher: current_user)` with `def initialize(post, publisher:)`.
- You SHOULD NOT pass a record with unsaved changes to an action, e.g. `post.title = title` then `Posts::PublishPost.call(post, publisher: current_user)`. Save the changes first, or pass the new values as keywords and set them in the action, e.g. `Posts::PublishPost.call(post, publisher: current_user, title:)`. Break this only when the action's task is to save a new record the caller built, e.g. `Posts::CopyPost` saving a copy built with `post.duplicate_post`, with copies of its associations.
- You MUST NOT build a query on a record's association in more than one step in an action, e.g. `post.comments.where(locked: false)`. Call a read method on the model instead, following the models instructions, e.g. `post.unlocked_comments.update_all(locked: true, updated_at: Time.zone.now)`, not `post.comments.unlocked.update_all(...)`. Do the same for a query that starts from a class, e.g. `Comment.on_posts(posts)`, not `Comment.where(post: posts)`.
- When an action works on many records, pass the records and name the action in the plural, e.g. `Posts::ArchivePosts.call(author.posts)`. You MUST NOT pass their IDs. Work on every record given, and leave picking the records to the caller.
- Pass either a relation (or association) or an array of records to an action on many records, and pick one for each action. Pass the same kind from every caller, and you MUST NOT let the action accept both, e.g. by checking `posts.is_a?(Array)`. Prefer a relation when there could be many records.
- In an action on many records, write them in one statement when the task can be done in SQL and no callback, validation or `dependent:` on the model needs to run for the change, e.g. `posts.update_all(archived_at: now, updated_at: now)` with `now = Time.zone.now`, inside a transaction when it writes more than once. Update the relation's own records last, because each statement runs the relation's query again, e.g. `Comment.on_posts(posts).update_all(locked: true, updated_at: now)` before `posts.update_all(archived_at: now, updated_at: now)`.
- Always pass `updated_at` to `update_all`, e.g. `update_all(locked: true, updated_at: Time.zone.now)`, because `update_all` doesn't set it.
- When each record needs the model's validations, callbacks or a lock, load them with `find_each`, or loop with `each` over an array, and call the single-record action for each, e.g. `posts.find_each { |post| Posts::ArchivePost.call(post) }`. Avoid wrapping that loop in a transaction.
- Prefer `find_each` to `each` when you loop over a relation, e.g. `posts.find_each`, not `posts.each`.
- You MUST NOT authorise the user or validate user input in an action. Do both in the caller before it calls the action, e.g. `authorize @post` in the controller and validations in the form. Trust the caller, and do the task.
- To check an action's arguments, include `ValidatedCallable` from `app/actions/concerns/validated_callable.rb`, then validate them, e.g. `validates :post, :publisher, presence: true` in `Posts::PublishPost`.
- When an action checks that a record argument has no unsaved changes, use `unmodified: { allow_blank: true }`, e.g. `validates :post, presence: true, unmodified: { allow_blank: true }` in `Posts::PublishPost`.
- When an action needs a record argument to be saved, e.g. it passes the record to a job, validate it with `persisted: { allow_blank: true }`, e.g. `validates :post, presence: true, persisted: { allow_blank: true }` in `Posts::SendNewsletter`.
- You MUST NOT use an action's argument validations to control the app's flow. You MUST NOT rescue `ActiveModel::ValidationError` when you call an action, and you MUST NOT raise it again as the action's `Error`.
- You MUST NOT return a value from an action, and you MUST NOT use the value an action returns.
- When a caller needs a value from an action's work, have the action save it on a record the caller holds, and read it from the record after the call, e.g. `@post.newsletter_id` after `Posts::SendNewsletter.call(@post)`.
- When another service accepts an ID from you, generate the ID in the caller and pass it to the action, e.g. `newsletter_id = SecureRandom.uuid` then `Posts::SendNewsletter.call(@post, newsletter_id:)`.
- When an API client tracks a request to another service, create a record for the request first with your own ID, e.g. `has_secure_token :reference` on `NewsletterDelivery`. Send your ID to the service, and give the client your ID, not the service's.
- You MUST NOT pass a value back from an action through a block or a result object, e.g. `Posts::SendNewsletter.call(post) { |newsletter_id| ... }` or `Result.new(success: true, value: response.id)`.
- For more ways to get a value from an action's work, see https://bmorrall.github.io/happy_rails/patterns/values-from-actions/.
- When an action's task fails, raise an error, e.g. with `update!`, rather than returning `false`.
- Let an error that no caller is meant to handle pass through the action unchanged.
- When a caller is meant to handle an error, define a custom `Error` class inside the action that inherits from `StandardError`, e.g. `class Error < StandardError; end` in `Posts::ArchivePost`. In `call`, rescue the errors the caller is meant to handle and raise them again as the action's `Error`, e.g. `rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e` then `raise Error, e.message`.
- When an action can fail for more than one cause and callers handle the causes differently, give each cause its own error class that inherits from the action's `Error`, e.g. `class RejectedError < Error; end` and `class ServiceError < Error; end` in `Posts::SendNewsletter`. Callers rescue the class for the cause they handle, or `Error` for them all.
- When another service fails, e.g. it returns a 500 or times out, raise the action's error class for that cause, e.g. `ServiceError`, from the client's base error class, after the `rescue` for causes the user can fix, e.g. `rescue NewsletterClient::UnprocessableError` then `rescue NewsletterClient::Error => e` and `raise ServiceError, e.message`.
- When several actions call the same service for related tasks and their callers handle each cause the same way, you MAY define their error classes once in a base class for the group. Inherit it from `ApplicationAction`, and name it after the group, ending in `Action`, e.g. `Posts::NewsletterAction` in `app/actions/posts/newsletter_action.rb`. Inherit each action from it, e.g. `class SendPrivateNewsletter < NewsletterAction`, and leave out the action's own error classes.
- An action that shares its errors through a base class SHOULD NOT define error classes. Put every class the group raises in the base class, e.g. `class ServiceError < Error; end` in `Posts::NewsletterAction`.
- The base class for shared errors MAY turn the service's errors into the group's in a private method that takes a block, named `with_` and the group's errors, e.g. `def with_newsletter_errors` with `yield`, then `rescue NewsletterClient::UnprocessableError => e` and `raise RejectedError, e.message`, then `rescue NewsletterClient::Error => e` and `raise ServiceError, e.message`, in `Posts::NewsletterAction`. Wrap only the service call in the block, e.g. `newsletter = with_newsletter_errors { NewsletterClient.new.create_private_newsletter(title: post.title, body: post.body) }` then `post.update!(newsletter_id: newsletter.id)`.
- When one action that shares its errors needs a finer cause, it MAY add a subclass of a shared cause, e.g. `class TimeoutError < ServiceError; end` in `Posts::SendPrivateNewsletter`. When the group has a `with_` method, rescue the finer cause inside its block, e.g. `rescue NewsletterClient::TimeoutError => e` then `raise TimeoutError, e.message`.
- You MUST NOT inherit an error class in an action that shares its errors from the base class's `Error`, e.g. `class NewCauseError < Error; end` or `class Error < BaseAction::Error; end`. When an action needs a new cause, add its class to the base class.
- Rescue shared errors by the base class's name, e.g. `rescue Posts::NewsletterAction::RejectedError`, not by the name of the action you called.
- Share errors only when no caller needs to know which action in the group failed. Actions that share errors MUST NOT call each other. Call them in turn from a form or a job.
- When an action writes more than once, wrap the writes in `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction` inside the action, e.g. `post.update!(archived_at: Time.zone.now)` and `post.comments.update_all(locked: true, updated_at: Time.zone.now)` in `Posts::ArchivePost`. You MUST NOT open a transaction in an action that writes once.
- When an action relies on a lock, take it inside the action with `with_lock`, e.g. `post.with_lock do ... end` in `Posts::PublishPost`. You MUST NOT take the lock in the caller.
- When an action that locks a record needs new values, set them inside the `with_lock` block, not before it.
- You MAY check a condition before taking a lock, to skip the lock when the work is not needed, e.g. `return if post.published?`. Always check it again inside the lock, e.g. `next if post.published?` as the first line of the `with_lock` block.
- Use `next` to leave a `transaction` or `with_lock` block early. You MUST NOT use `return` inside the block.
- When a check before or inside a lock fails, do nothing if the work is already done, e.g. the post is already published. Raise the action's `Error` when the caller needs to know, e.g. to show a form error. Do the same in both checks.
- When an action locks more than one record, lock them in the same order every time, the parent before its children, e.g. the post before its comments.
- You MUST NOT call another service inside a transaction, e.g. `NewsletterClient.new.create_newsletter(title: post.title, body: post.body)`. Call it first, then save its reply in the transaction, e.g. `post.update!(newsletter_id: response.id)`.
- When an action needs another service's reply, include `NonTransactionalCallable` from `app/actions/concerns/non_transactional_callable.rb`, e.g. `include NonTransactionalCallable` in `Posts::SendNewsletter`. You MUST NOT call such an action inside a transaction.
- When an action does not need another service's reply, you MUST NOT call the service from the action. Enqueue a job that calls it instead, e.g. `NotifySubscribersJob.perform_later(post)`, with `self.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = true` in the job class.
- When a call to another service needs to be retried if it fails, run it in a job of its own that does nothing else, e.g. `NotifySubscribersJob`. When a user is waiting for the reply, call the action directly and you MUST NOT retry it automatically.
- Run work that needs to wait for the commit and is not a job, e.g. a Turbo broadcast, in an `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit` block, e.g. `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit { post.broadcast_refresh }`. You MUST NOT rely on running it after the action's own transaction block.
- You MUST NOT raise `ActiveRecord::Rollback` in an action. Raise a real error, so the whole transaction rolls back.
- Rescue errors to raise them again as the action's `Error` outside the transaction block, e.g. with a `rescue` on `call`, including another action's errors. You MUST NOT rescue an error inside a `transaction` or `with_lock` block and carry on.
- Start the name of an action whose write needs to stay saved when other work fails with `Record`, e.g. `Posts::RecordLinkCheck` saves `link_check_status` on the post.
- You MUST NOT call a `Record` action inside a transaction, including a nested `requires_new: true` block. Call it before or after the transaction block, e.g. `Posts::RecordLinkCheck.call(post)` before `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do`. Read its result from the record, e.g. `return false if post.link_check_failed?`.
- Include `NonTransactionalCallable` in every `Record` action, e.g. `include NonTransactionalCallable` in `Posts::RecordLinkCheck`.
